description.narrative:
The United Network of Young Peacebuilders (UNOY) is a youth-led network that unites around 130 organisations in almost 70 countries who work on youth-led peacebuilding, in line with Security Council Resolutions 2250, 2419 and 2535 on Youth, Peace and Security (YPS).
Through advocacy and its acknowledged role, UNOY has been able to influence global policy through informed local experiences and have this way contributed to driving the YPS agenda forward at global, regional and national levels. Apart from being part of setting youth-led peacebuilding on the agenda, UNOY co-chairs the Global Coalition on YPS together with the UN, with more than 100 members from the UN and civil society.
Six Regional Coordinators capture regional priorities and needs under the network’s Strategic Plan for 2021-2025. The plan includes five change goals to protect young peacebuilders and the civic space they work in, resource youth-led peacebuilding sustainably, ensure their meaningful participation and equal partnership and support creative changemaking in order to create a world ‘free from all forms of violence, where young people have the power to transform conflicts, youth participation is real and meaningful for all, and young people actively partner for peace without fear or threat’.
Sida has provided core support through the UNOY Secretariat in The Hague since 2018.

United Network of Young Peacebuilders (UNOY) är ett ungdomslett nätverk som samlar runt 130 organisationer som arbetar med ungas fredsbyggande från närmare 70 länder, i enlighet med Säkerhetsrådsresolutionerna 2250, 2419 och 2535 om Unga, fred och säkerhet (YPS).
Genom påverkansarbete och i rollen som ett internationellt erkänt nätverk har UNOY kunnat influera global policy genom att bidra med lokala erfarenheter som i sin tur hjälpt driva YPS agendan framåt på global, regional och nationell nivå. Utöver att ha deltagit vid framtagandet av YPS-agendan så är UNOY även med och leder den Globala koalitionen för YPS tillsammans med FN, där över 100 medlemmar från FN och civilsamhället är med.
Sex regionala samordnare lyfter regionsspecifika prioriteringar och utmaningar utifrån nätverkets Strategiska plan för 2021-2025. Planen innehåller fem förändringsmål för att skydda unga fredsbyggare och det civila utrymme de arbetar i, söka hållbara resurser för ungas fredsbyggande, säkra meningsfullt deltagande och jämlikt partnerskap samt stötta kreativa förändringar för att uppnå en värld som är ’fri från allt våld, där unga människor har möjlighet att transformera konflikt, där ungas deltagande är säkerställd och meningsfull för alla, och där unga människor aktivt deltar i fredsbyggande utan rädsla eller hot’.
Sida har bidragit med kärnstöd genom UNOYs sekretariat i Haag sedan 2018.

description.narrative:
UNOY has in their 2025 reported on cummulative results from their 2024 activities and implementation of their Strategic Plan. Some results are highlighted below (for full overview of results, see the UNOY annual 2025 report dox xx?):
- The number of members of UNOY increased to a total 120 from 70 different countries (compared to 111 members in 64 countries in 2023), reaching over 19 million people (directly and indirectly) through their local members' work. Around 310 people received training and capacity building during 2024 with 93% of the participants reporting being better quipped to carry out peace-building work as a result of their participation in UNOY's trainings.
- At national level, the International Secretariat (IS) supported UNOY members in strengthening their advocacy work for YPS. In 2024, this led to a number of positive outcomes in relation to localisation of the Youth, Peace and Security (YPS) Agenda. Across several countries, UNOY members played key roles in developing National Action Plans (NAPs) on YPS, ensuring that you people were not only consulted but actively shaping national policy processes.
- In the Gambia, UNOY member 'Peace Hub' worked closely with the Ministry for Youth and Sport and co-organised YPS trainings for the National Assembly, local government officials, the National Youth Council and local communities. Peace Hub's work culminated in their participation in the NAP validation process alongside government, multilateral, and civil society actors in December 2024.
- In Burundi, the 'Youth Empowerment and Leadership Initiative (YELI)', also a member of UNOY, was nominated by the government to join the the Steering Committee for the creation of the country's NAP, participating in multiple rounds of consultation and the development process which was finalised in 2024.
Both Peace Hub and YELI have been long-term members of the UNOY's Africa Youth Advocacy Team (A-YAT) and participated in the UNOY activities such as the 'Young Peacebuilders Forum 2023', A-YAT Advocacy trainings, as well as peer-learning sessions on the topic of YPS implementation. Through evaluation, it was reported that they had utilised the knowledge, skills and visibility gained through active participation in UNOY's activities. This has also been the case for a number of members involved in national YPS implementation processes in countries such as Iraq, Liberia, Ghana and Kenya, among others.
- Sida's core flexible funding to UNOY has has also enabled the IS to support members across the global network and to be guided by their members' needs and priorities. Rather than having set topics and trainings in advance for member organisations the Sida core funding has enabled UNOY to invest time in co-developing activities jointly with members to ensures these are responsive to their needs, priorities and situations in the national and local contexts. For example, in 2024 members in the Europe and MENA region decided to have a cross-regional forum to foster solidarity between the two regions and learn from one another. The activity led to increased cooperation and solidarity amongst the members in the two regions, with them actively exploring opportunities to collaborate on for example, joint funding opportunities for local initiatives in their respective regions/countries of origin.
- Sida's core funding has also enabled UNOY to establish a limited emergency fund providing support for emergency relocation, psychosocial support, and legal assistance to members at risk. Given the shrinking civic space globally, UNOY has seen an increase in the amount of member representatives reaching out for this type of assistance. In 2024, members reached out nine times to UNOY staff for assistance, and in six of these cases the emergency protection fund was leveraged to support members located in the Democratic Republic of Congo, Haiti, Venezuela, South Sudan and Uganda.
- Given the nature of the core support, it is also important for Sida to assess progresses in relation to organisational development of UNOY and its' central functions, such as the network membership, the IS and more. In the annual review, UNOY has reported that their main achievements in 2024 under these areas have been strengthened internal communication within the network and between the International Secretariat and the network, which resulted in higher levels of coordination and collaboration between members and coordination ahead of for example advocacy engagements. UNOY has also continued to focus on decentralisation in 2024, with the increase of stipends to the Regional Coordinators (RCs) to strengthen their roles, with the results of increased partnerships with regional UN entities, INGO's and regional networks. A central work during 2024 has also been the development of UNOY's 2026-2030 Strategic Plan, using a participatory approach to ensure it reflects members priorities.
